# P5 Cross-Implementation Report Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Publish `conformance/REPORT.md`, the cross-implementation matrix REQ-CONF-8 names, regenerated by CI with the `-update` golden pattern; and complete `conformance/DRAFT-GAPS.md` (REQ-CONF-9) with a gap entry for every behavior the vectors had to choose that the draft leaves open, each cross-referenced to the third parties that diverge on it. Three third-party implementations run in pinned containers: `hono-idempotency` 0.9.1, `github.com/eben-vranken/idempo` v1.0.0 and `github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3/middleware/idempotency` v3.5.0. Every failing core vector gets an issue draft in the repository. Nothing is sent anywhere.

**Architecture:** The suite already exists and is transport-only (D18): the TypeScript runner drives a fetch handler or a base URL, the Go runner drives an `http.Handler` or a base URL. P5 adds no semantics. It adds three things. First, a *target*: a small fixture app per third-party implementation, written by us, mounting the REQ-CONF-2 fixture contract behind that implementation's middleware, built into a container from pinned registry packages (design note C2, never `git clone`). Second, a *collector*: one script that runs every row of the matrix, normalizes each run into a committed JSON result, and refuses to differ from what is committed unless `--update` is given. Third, a *renderer*: a pure function from the row manifest plus the results to the markdown of `REPORT.md`, so the golden file can be checked in a job with no containers at all. The gap list is prose derived from the vectors and from what the three runs actually showed.

**Tech Stack:** Bun 1.2.21 local (CI Bun latest 1.4.x), TypeScript 5 strict, Biome 2, Docker Compose v2 with a second compose file at `conformance/third-party/compose.yml`, base images `node:22.23.2-alpine` and `golang:1.26.8-alpine3.24`, `hono-idempotency@0.9.1` with `hono@4.13.8`, `hono-problem-details@0.11.0` and `@hono/node-server@2.1.1`, `github.com/eben-vranken/idempo v1.0.0`, `github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3 v3.5.0`, Go 1.26 for `go/cmd/conformance`, wrangler 4.x (`wrangler dev --local`) for the Durable Objects and D1 rows, the existing `test/compose.yml` services for the DynamoDB, Redis and Postgres rows.

**Spec:** `requirements.md` sections 0.2, 0.4 (S3, S4), 2 (D17, D18, D20), 4.7 (REQ-CONF-8, REQ-CONF-9), 4.9 (REQ-REL-4); `docs/superpowers/questions.md` Q1, Q9, Q14 and the new Q50 to Q53 (Task 1); `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-anyonce-design.md` items A3 and C2; `conformance/README.md` (the fixture contract and the `short-ttl` capability); `CHECKLIST.md` sections "Every phase" and "P5 cross-implementation report".

## Global Constraints

- Prose in docs, comments, commit messages, changeset text, YAML, Dockerfiles and shell: no em or en dashes (U+2013, U+2014). Gate: `rg -n "[\x{2013}\x{2014}]" --glob '!node_modules' --glob '!*.lock' --glob '!docs/reference/**' .` returns nothing. This includes the generated `conformance/REPORT.md`, so the renderer must never emit one.
- Test names start with the REQ id they prove: `REQ-CONF-8: renderReport gives every target one row`. There are exactly two REQ ids in this phase, CONF-8 and CONF-9; `bun run scripts/reqs.ts --phase p5` must be green in the last task.
- TypeScript: `strict`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` (build objects conditionally, never assign `undefined` to an optional property), `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, no `any` outside test fakes. The report tooling lives under `scripts/` and may use `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:process` and `Bun.spawn`; it is not published and adds no dependency to any `@anyonce/*` package.
- No published package gains a dependency in this phase. `@anyonce/conformance` is untouched except for anything Task 4 proves it already does. The third-party fixture apps are not workspace packages and are never installed into the root `bun.lock`; they are built only inside their containers with their own lockfiles.
- No `git clone` anywhere, in CI or in a Dockerfile (design note C2). Every third-party dependency arrives from `registry.npmjs.org` or `proxy.golang.org` at an exact version. Every base image is pinned to an exact patch tag. Every one of those versions and tags appears in `conformance/REPORT.md`.
- `conformance/REPORT.md` is deterministic: no timestamps, no host names, no ports, no durations, rows in manifest order, vectors in catalog order. A rerun on an unchanged tree produces a byte-identical file. The committed `conformance/results/*.json` are the same run summaries with `target` and `generatedAt` stripped.
- Third-party implementations are graded on the `core` tier only (D17). Their `profile` numbers appear in the matrix as information and never as a pass or fail judgement, and the report says so in the sentence above the table.
- `requires: ["short-ttl"]` is declared for a target only when that target is configured with a record TTL of at most 2000 ms. Where it cannot be, `core/expiry-executes-again` is reported `not-applicable`, which is the honest grade and is counted in the N/A column, never as a failure.
- A fixture app is the smallest wiring that satisfies `conformance/README.md`'s fixture contract. It never works around the implementation under test: no retry, no key rewriting, no status translation. Any configuration that departs from the implementation's own defaults is named in `REPORT.md` next to the row and justified there (Q53).
- No external action. Nothing is opened, filed, posted or published on any repository or list. `conformance/issues/*.md` are drafts in this repository and their front matter says so.
- Never log a full key; nothing this phase adds logs a key at all, so the key-log gate `rg -n 'console\.(log|info|warn|error)\(.*key' packages go` stays empty. The third-party fixture apps live outside `packages` and `go`, and still must not log a key.
- Go: `go/cmd/conformance` and the `-store` flag on `go/cmd/fixture` use the standard library plus the store clients already in `go/go.mod`; no new module requirement; no cgo; errors wrapped with `%w`; doc comments on exported identifiers; `go vet`, `go test -race`, `golangci-lint run` clean. Run Go as `GOROOT= /opt/homebrew/bin/go <verb> -C go ./...`; golangci-lint as `GOROOT= sh -c 'cd go && golangci-lint run'`; the engine coverage gate as `GOROOT= GO=/opt/homebrew/bin/go scripts/go-engine-coverage.sh` (still 100 percent; this phase does not touch `engine.go`).
- Conventional commits: `feat(conformance): ...`, `feat(go): ...`, `test(conformance): ...`, `docs(conformance): ...`, `ci: ...`. Commit after every task. Git only as plain single commands from the worktree root (no `cd`, no `&&` between git commands, no `-C`).
- Never write a `\uXXXX` escape inside a tool parameter; the editing tools decode it into the raw character. Use `\x` escapes or named escapes.
- Shared files are touched additively so the parallel P4b branch rebases cleanly: root `package.json` (one script line plus the `test` filter), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (three steps appended to the existing `services` job, no new job), `test/ci.test.ts` (one new test, no edit to the existing job-name array), `.gitignore` (one line), `CHECKLIST.md` (the P5 section only), `docs/superpowers/questions.md` (append only).
- No changeset: this phase changes no published package's public API. Task 8 states that in the integration PR body instead.

## Decisions taken in this plan (not spec changes)

- **The report gate is a step in the existing `services` job, not a new CI job.** `test/ci.test.ts` asserts the exact set of job names, a file P4b may also touch; appending steps to `services` avoids editing that array. It is also the job that already has Docker, Bun, Go, a built workspace and the `test/compose.yml` stack up, which the anyonce DynamoDB, Redis and Postgres rows need. The brief allows either shape.
- **Two gates, one golden file.** `conformance/results/*.json` are committed alongside `conformance/REPORT.md`. The cheap gate runs in the `ts` job with no containers: render from the committed results and compare to the committed `REPORT.md`. The real gate runs in `services`: re-run every target, compare the fresh results to the committed ones, then compare the render to the committed `REPORT.md`. `--update` rewrites both. This is D20's `-update` pattern with the property that a reader can regenerate the report from what is in the repository.
- **Durable Objects and D1 rows come from `wrangler dev --local`.** Those two stores only exist inside workerd and the workers test pool has no filesystem, so a summary cannot be written from inside it. `wrangler dev --local` serves a worker that mounts the fixture behind `withIdempotency` with either store, over HTTP, and the URL runner drives it like any other target. wrangler is already a pinned devDependency. D1's schema is applied by calling the store's own `ensureSchema(db)` on first request, so no migration command is needed. Fallback if `wrangler dev` proves unusable in the task's budget: drive the same worker with `Miniflare` from the collector process. Second fallback: render both rows as `not-run` with the reason and a pointer to `packages/stores/workers/*.test.ts`, and file it as a Q entry.
- **Third-party rows are driven by the TypeScript CLI, with one vector regraded by the Go runner.** `conformance/README.md` already records that `core/header-name-case-insensitive` cannot discriminate from the TypeScript runner, because `Headers` lowercases every field name it is given, so a TypeScript run reports a pass that proves nothing. `go/cmd/conformance` is added as the URL-mode Go CLI and that one vector's result for every third-party row comes from it. `REPORT.md` names the runner per vector where they differ. Recorded as Q52.
- **The Fiber fixture overrides two defaults and the report says so.** Fiber's default `KeyHeader` is `X-Idempotency-Key`, which is not the field the draft defines, and its default `KeyHeaderValidate` rejects any key that is not exactly 36 characters by returning a bare `error`, which Fiber's default error handler turns into 500. With the defaults every vector errors and the run measures nothing. The fixture sets `KeyHeader: "Idempotency-Key"` and a permissive validator. Both the non-draft default header and the 500-instead-of-400 validation path become findings in the Fiber issue drafts rather than being hidden by the override. Recorded as Q53.
- **Every third party can declare `short-ttl`, so `core/expiry-executes-again` is graded for all three.** `hono-idempotency` takes `memoryStore({ ttl: 2000 })` in milliseconds; `idempo` takes `inmem.New(2*time.Second, 2*time.Second)`; Fiber takes `Lifetime: 2 * time.Second`, which is its practical floor because it stores whole seconds. No N/A is expected on the third-party rows for that vector, and if one appears it is reported, not worked around.
- **The Go third-party containers are single stage.** `golang:1.26.8-alpine3.24` builds and runs. A multi-stage build would save image size that nothing in this phase measures, and costs a second pinned base image.
- **Issue drafts live at `conformance/issues/<implementation>-<vector-name>.md`.** `REPORT.md` links to them relatively, so the matrix is self-contained wherever `conformance/` is read. `CHECKLIST.md` is amended to match; `docs/standards/` still holds S1 to S3 in P7. Recorded as Q50.
- **The row manifest is code, not data.** `scripts/report/rows.ts` exports a typed `ROWS` array. A row that has no committed result, or a committed result with no row, is an error in both directions, so the matrix cannot silently shrink.
- **anyonce's own rows are graded on `core` and `profile` both.** D17's core-only rule exists so third parties are not judged on anyonce's profile choices. anyonce is judged on everything.

## File Structure

```

conformance/third-party/hono-idempotency/app.mjs         fixture contract behind idempotency({ store: memoryStore({ ttl: 2000 }), required: true, ... })

.github/workflows/ci.yml                                 three steps appended to the services job
```

Branch `p5-scaffold`. No code.

- [ ] Append Q50 to Q53 to `docs/superpowers/questions.md` in the existing format (heading, body, `Recommended resolution:`, `**Decision: pending.** P5 proceeds on the recommendation.`).
- [ ] Amend the `CHECKLIST.md` P5 section's fourth item to `S4 issue drafts in \`conformance/issues/\` (not opened)`, per Q50. Leave the other three items alone.
- [ ] Correct the three third-party rows of the `requirements.md` 0.2 prior-art table per Q51, with the verified versions, publication dates and store lists, and add the verification date. Precedent: Q1's decision corrected the same table.

Q text to write, verbatim in substance:

**Q50: the P5 issue drafts have two homes in the spec.** `CHECKLIST.md`'s P5 section says "S4 issue drafts in `docs/standards/issues/` (not opened)". REQ-CONF-8 says each failing vector links to a filed issue, and the link lives in `conformance/REPORT.md`. Recommended resolution: the drafts live at `conformance/issues/<implementation>-<vector-name>.md` so `REPORT.md` can link to them relatively and the whole matrix is readable from inside `conformance/`; `CHECKLIST.md` is amended to match. `docs/standards/` is created in P7 for S1, S2 and S3, which are documents about the draft rather than about an implementation.

**Q51: requirements 0.2 names versions and stores that the registries no longer show.** Verified on 18 September 2026: `hono-idempotency` is at 0.9.1 (published 18 July 2026), not 0.9.0 (May 2026), and its stores are memory, Cloudflare KV, D1, Durable Objects and Redis. "idempo" resolves to `github.com/eben-vranken/idempo` v1.0.0 (2 June 2026), whose stores are in-memory, Redis and Postgres, not "in-memory (others unclear)"; it is RFC 9457 problem details throughout, returns 409 and 422, and sets `Idempotency-Replayed`. The Fiber middleware's current home is `github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3/middleware/idempotency` at v3.5.0. Recommended resolution: run the report against those versions, record every one of them in `REPORT.md`, and correct the 0.2 rows now so the P7 case study is not built on stale facts. The 0.3 novelty claim is unaffected: none of the three has a queue or webhook door and none ships conformance vectors.

**Q52: `core/header-name-case-insensitive` cannot be graded by the TypeScript runner.** `conformance/README.md` already records that the `Headers` class lowercases every field name, so the TypeScript runner cannot put a differently spelled name on the wire and the vector reports a pass that proves nothing. Grading a third party on it from a CLI run would therefore be false. Recommended resolution: add `go/cmd/conformance`, the URL-mode Go CLI (the Go runner sets `req.Header[name]` directly and does put the lowercase spelling on the wire), and take that one vector's result for every third-party row from it. Every other vector comes from `bunx @anyonce/conformance --url` as REQ-CONF-7 says. `REPORT.md` names the runner for that vector.

**Q53: the Fiber middleware cannot be measured on its defaults.** Its default `KeyHeader` is `X-Idempotency-Key`, not the field the draft defines, and its default `KeyHeaderValidate` rejects any key that is not exactly 36 characters by returning a bare `error`, which Fiber's default error handler renders as 500. On the defaults every vector errors on the key and the run measures the fixture, not the middleware. Recommended resolution: the Fiber fixture sets `KeyHeader: "Idempotency-Key"` and a permissive `KeyHeaderValidate`; `REPORT.md` prints both overrides in the row's notes; and the two defaults become findings in the Fiber issue drafts (the header name is a draft-conformance gap, the 500 is an error-handling gap against draft section 2.7, which asks for 400). Without the overrides the row would say "0/11 core, every vector errored", which is true and useless.

### Task 2: Third-party containers and the fixture contract

Branch `p5-containers`. TDD is inverted here: the test is the conformance suite itself, so write the compose file and one container at a time and prove each answers the fixture contract before moving on.

The fixture contract is `conformance/README.md`'s table and must be reproduced exactly in every app: `POST /echo` 201 echoing the body bytes and content type (default `application/octet-stream`), `POST /status/{code}` with body `status:{code}` as `text/plain`, `POST /slow?ms=N` waiting N ms then 200 with `slept:N`, `POST /large?bytes=N` 200 with N bytes of `x` as `application/octet-stream`, `GET /counter` 200 `{"count":n}` behind the layer, `POST /reset` 204 outside the layer. Every POST fixture increments one process-global counter. Read the two reference apps first: `conformance/fixtures/hono/src/app.ts` and `go/conformance/fixture`.

- [ ] `conformance/third-party/hono-idempotency/`: `package.json` pinning `hono-idempotency@0.9.1`, `hono@4.13.8`, `hono-problem-details@0.11.0`, `@hono/node-server@2.1.1` with exact versions and no ranges; `app.mjs` with the contract, `app.post('/reset', ...)` registered before `app.use('*', idempotency({...}))` so the control endpoint stays outside the layer; options `{ store: memoryStore({ ttl: 2000, sweepInterval: 500 }), headerName: 'Idempotency-Key', required: true, methods: ['POST','PUT','PATCH','DELETE'], dangerouslyAllowGlobalKeys: true }`; `serve({ fetch: app.fetch, port: 3000, hostname: '0.0.0.0' })`. `Dockerfile` from `node:22.23.2-alpine`, `npm ci` against a committed `package-lock.json` generated in the container build context, `EXPOSE 3000`, `CMD ["node", "app.mjs"]`.
- [ ] `conformance/third-party/idempo/`: `go.mod` `module anyonce.local/fixture/idempo`, `go 1.26.3`, `require github.com/eben-vranken/idempo v1.0.0`, with a committed `go.sum`; `main.go` building `http.NewServeMux()` with the contract handlers, `store := inmem.New(2*time.Second, 2*time.Second)`, `mw := idempo.New(store, idempo.Options{})`, and an outer mux that routes `POST /reset` to the bare handler and everything else through `mw.Handler(inner)`. `Dockerfile` from `golang:1.26.8-alpine3.24`, `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go build`, `EXPOSE 3000`.
- [ ] `conformance/third-party/fiber/`: `go.mod` `module anyonce.local/fixture/fiber`, `require github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3 v3.5.0`, committed `go.sum`; `main.go` with `app.Post("/reset", ...)` registered before `app.Use(idempotency.New(idempotency.Config{ Lifetime: 2 * time.Second, KeyHeader: "Idempotency-Key", KeyHeaderValidate: func(string) error { return nil } }))`, then the contract routes. The counter is an `atomic.Int64`. `Dockerfile` from `golang:1.26.8-alpine3.24`.
- [ ] `conformance/third-party/compose.yml`: `name: anyonce-third-party`; services `hono-idempotency` on host port 13001, `idempo` on 13002, `fiber` on 13003, each `build:` its directory, each with a health check that hits `POST /reset` (the one endpoint every target answers identically) or `GET /counter`, `interval: 2s`, `retries: 30`. No shared network beyond the default, no volumes.
- [ ] `conformance/third-party/README.md`: one paragraph per container naming the package and version, the configuration chosen and why (Q53 for Fiber), how to run one by hand (`docker compose -f conformance/third-party/compose.yml up -d --wait hono-idempotency` then `bun run conformance -- --url http://127.0.0.1:13001 --tier core --report markdown`), and the rule that a fixture never works around the implementation under test.

### Task 4: The row manifest, the renderer and the golden test

Branch `p5-generator`. Strict TDD: the renderer is a pure function and every test below runs without a container.

- [ ] `scripts/report/rows.ts`:

```ts
export type RowKind = 'ts-in-process' | 'ts-url' | 'go-url' | 'workerd-url';
export interface ReportRow {
  /** Stable id; also the results file name. */
  id: string;
  implementation: string;
  /** Exact published version, or "this repo" for anyonce. */
  version: string;
  language: 'TypeScript' | 'Go';
  store: string;
  kind: RowKind;
  /** Graded tiers. Third parties are core only (D17). */
  graded: readonly ('core' | 'profile')[];
  capabilities: readonly 'short-ttl'[];
  /** Pinned container image, when this row runs in one. */
  image?: string;
  /** Pinned package versions installed in the container. */
  packages?: readonly string[];
  /** Configuration that departs from the implementation's defaults, and why. */
  notes?: string;
}
export const ROWS: readonly ReportRow[];
```

### Task 7: Complete `conformance/DRAFT-GAPS.md` (REQ-CONF-9)

Branch `p5-gaps`. No code.

Keep the existing preamble, the editor's copy delta and G1 to G3 as they are, and keep the entry format. Add one entry per open point, each in the committed format plus a new `Third parties that diverge:` line naming the implementations and the vector results from `REPORT.md` that show it. Every vector id under `conformance/vectors/` must appear in at least one entry; Task 4's test enforces that. The entries to write, at minimum:

- **G4 replay indication.** Section 2.6. The draft says a retry after completion gets the previous result and names no way for the client to know it was replayed. anyonce sets `Idempotency-Replayed: true` (D10), vector `profile/replayed-header`. Propose a registered response header field.
- **G5 concurrent duplicate signalling.** Section 2.7 asks for 409 and says the client need not correct the request, but gives no way to say when to retry. anyonce sends `Retry-After` from the lease remaining, minimum 1 second (D10), vectors `core/concurrent-409`, `profile/retry-after-on-409`. Propose that a 409 SHOULD carry `Retry-After`.
- **G6 what a 5xx original does to the key.** Section 2.6 says the resource replays "success or an error", which read literally pins a 500 for the life of the key. Every deployed implementation surveyed abandons instead. anyonce stores status below 500 and abandons otherwise (D6), vector `profile/5xx-not-stored`. Propose text that distinguishes a result the resource chose from a failure it suffered.
- **G7 4xx originals are replayed.** The same sentence, the other side: anyonce does replay a stored 4xx, vector `profile/4xx-replayed`. Propose that 4xx be named explicitly as replayable.
- **G8 sf-string versus bare token.** Section 2.1 requires an RFC 8941 String, so a bare token is a syntax error, yet none of the three third parties parses the field as a structured field and all of them treat `"abc"` and `abc` as different keys. anyonce defaults to `lenient` and offers `strict` (D7), vector `core/sf-string-quoted-key`. Propose either a normative parsing requirement with a stated error status or an explicit allowance of bare tokens, and note that the reference should be RFC 9651.
- **G9 maximum key length.** The draft sets none. anyonce rejects over 255 bytes with 400 (D7, Q9 moved the vector to `profile`), vector `profile/key-too-long`. `idempo` also uses 255; `hono-idempotency` uses 256 characters. Propose a stated minimum a resource must accept.
- **G10 fingerprint scope and the mismatch status.** Section 2.4 lists fingerprint approaches and mandates none; section 2.7 says 422 for a reused key with a different payload but does not say what "different" covers. anyonce hashes method, path with query, and body bytes (D9), vector `core/mismatch-422`. `idempo` omits the query string; `hono-idempotency` keys the store by method and path, so a reuse across paths is not a mismatch at all but a new record; Fiber does not fingerprint. Propose that the draft state the minimum the fingerprint must cover.
- **G11 a rejected mismatch must not poison the key.** The draft is silent on the state of the record after a 422. anyonce leaves the original replayable, vector `core/mismatch-does-not-poison`. Propose text.
- **G12 expiry behavior.** Section 2.3 says the resource MAY require time based keys and SHOULD publish the policy; it does not say what happens to a request arriving after expiry. anyonce executes it as a first-time request, vector `core/expiry-executes-again`. Propose text, and propose that the policy be discoverable rather than only documented.
- **G13 scope of uniqueness.** Section 2.2 makes the key unique and section 5 recommends composite keys, but nothing says whether two different resources may see the same key. anyonce requires an explicit scope and defaults it to method plus route pattern with an optional principal (D8), vectors `core/two-keys-execute-twice`, `core/get-ignored`. Propose that the draft define the default scope.
- **G14 response size and the omitted body.** The draft never bounds the stored response. anyonce stores up to 1 MiB and replays status and headers with the body omitted above the cap (REQ-STORE-11, Q17), vector `profile/omitted-body-replay`. Propose that the draft acknowledge the bound and say what a resource does past it.
- **G15 a machine-readable error code.** Section 2.7's examples carry `type`, `title` and `detail` and no stable code. anyonce adds `code` (D11), vector `profile/problem-code-member`. Related to G1 and cross-referenced to it.
- **G16 the structured fields reference.** Both texts cite RFC 8941, obsoleted by RFC 9651 in September 2024. Already an observation in the editor's copy delta; promote it to a numbered entry so S3 can cite it.
- **G17 whether a resource may require the key.** Section 2.7 says "for a documented idempotent operation requiring this header", so requiring it is allowed, but section 2.5.1 says a general client cannot assume the server respects the header. Two of the three third parties cannot require it at all. anyonce's `required` defaults per adapter, vector `core/key-missing-required`. Propose that the draft say a resource MAY require the header and MUST document it.

Each entry ends with `Status: open`. None is filed.

**Verification:**

- [ ] Commit `docs(conformance): complete DRAFT-GAPS.md with G4 to G17 and the third-party divergences`.

## Self-review notes

- The one genuine unknown is Task 5. Everything else runs in a process this repository already knows how to start.
- The report is only as honest as the fixtures. A reviewer should read all three fixture apps against `conformance/README.md`'s table before reading a single number, and should check that no fixture retries, rewrites a key or translates a status.
- Expect the third-party rows to fail several core vectors. That is the deliverable, not a problem to fix. The temptation to tune a fixture until a row looks better is the main failure mode of this phase.
